The irrigation pump station is a critical component of the golf course and as such, it is necessary to maintain it in peak condition to ensure business continuity and optimal operating condition year round to avoid any potential disruptions. The Bridges at Springtree Golf Club is extremely busy and remains in high demand among many City residents and visitors.

m-winterhaven|nodate|75c2b32c|1c6654fe40.title: BACKGROUND Planned Unit Development Ordinance O-23-39 requires the developer of property located adjacent to Lake Ruby Drive, West, TJS of Central Florida, to construct roadway improvements from Eloise Loop Road/Thompson Nursery Road southward for a distance of approximately 1,300 feet to the entrance of their proposed residential development located south of Lake Ruby Drive, West and north of Lake Hart. The ordinance also requires the construction of a 2,400-foot long, 8-foot wide multi-purpose trail from the terminus of the improved roadway westward to County Road 653, across from Chain of Lakes Elementary School. Following Lake Ruby Drive, West’s transfer from Polk County’s ownership to the City’s ownership April 10, 2024, all improvements required by Planned Unit Development Ordinance O-23-39 were designed to the City’s roadway and utility standards. Earlier this year, the developer completed the required improvements to Lake Ruby Drive, West and is now requesting the City accept the constructed improvements. City staff conducted inspections of the improvements and found them ready for formal acceptance by the City. The value of the improvements is approximately $2,390,000. FIN

m-winterhaven|nodate|75c2b32c|20192983dc.title: BACKGROUND: In 2024, construction commenced on the primary phase of Chain of Lakes Park Phase II. A subsequent change order approved in November 2025 added an additional parking lot on the southwest side of the site. The Fieldhouse’s northwest parking lot has not been resurfaced in more than 20 years. Due to cost savings realized within the Chain of Lakes Park Phase II project, along with savings in the Parks and Recreation operating budget, there is an opportunity to engage the existing contractor, Rodda Construction, to complete the resurfacing while they remain mobilized on site. A budget amendment is required to authorize additional expenditures and the funding sources. The budget amendment reflected in Exhibit A is necessary to maintain compliance with F.S. 166.241 and Government Accounting Standards Board (GASB) requirements. FINANCIAL IMPACT: The requested amendment will transfer $110,000 from the General Fund to the Construction Fund for the proposed Change Order in the amount of $209,914.
